prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2005 – “Britain forward, not back” (Summary)

Core vision
- Apply enduring Labour values to modern priorities: opportunity and security for all.
- Build on stability and reform since 1997; reject “false choices” between economic dynamism and social justice.
- Embed a new progressive consensus: strong economy, high-quality universal public services, rights matched by responsibilities, and active international leadership.

Record since 1997
- Economy: Longest period of uninterrupted growth; lowest sustained interest/inflation for a generation; 2m more in work; minimum wage; tax credits; 1m+ more homeowners; poverty reduced among children and pensioners.
- Public services: Major investment; more teachers, nurses, doctors; big falls in heart disease and cancer deaths; primary school results among world’s best; free museum entry up visits 75%.
- Safety: Crime down ~30%; more police and CSOs; faster justice for young offenders.
- Global: Led on aid, EU enlargement and emissions trading; effective armed forces.

Third-term pledges and policies

Economy and work
- Maintain low debt, 2% inflation target, fiscal rules; no rise in basic/top income tax rates; protect VAT exemptions.
- Target 80% employment; raise minimum wage (£5.05 in 2005; £5.35 in 2006); reform incapacity benefit with support and obligations.
- Boost enterprise, skills and science (R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014); streamline regulation; back manufacturing and public procurement; £180bn+ transport investment to 2015; explore national road pricing.

Education and children
- Personalised learning; more teacher training/support; stronger basics; stretch the brightest.
- Every secondary to be an independent specialist school; 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future to renew all secondary and upgrade primaries.
- 14–19 reform with high-quality vocational diplomas; EMAs; expand apprenticeships and FE.
- Universal, affordable childcare: 3,500 Sure Start Children’s Centres; extended schools 8am–6pm; more free nursery hours.
- Parental support: paid maternity leave to 9 months (aim 12); extend flexible working rights; tackle child poverty (halve by 2010–11).

Health and social care
- NHS free and personal: 18-week referral-to-treatment by 2008; patient choice; expand primary/community services and modern community hospitals; use independent/voluntary capacity to add throughput; stronger hygiene/MRSA action.
- Public health: tighter school meal standards; clearer food labelling; restrict junk food marketing to children; widespread smoke-free legislation; expand cessation services.

Crime, borders and security
- Neighbourhood policing team in every community; 24,000 CSOs; single non-emergency number.
- Tougher action on antisocial behaviour, alcohol-related disorder, knives/guns; more drug testing/treatment linked to crime; restructure to tackle organised crime; reduce reoffending with end-to-end case management.
- Immigration: points-based system; English for settlement; employer penalties for illegal hiring; biometric visas, e-borders; ID cards linked to passports.

Older people, housing and communities
- Pension Credit maintained (linked to earnings to 2007–08); build long-term pensions consensus; flexible later-life work (end forced retirement before 65).
- Increase homeownership by up to 2m over three terms; more social homes and “Decent Homes” by 2010; choice-based lettings; tackle regional housing pressures.
- Devolve power: stronger local government with fewer targets/inspections, multi-year funding; neighbourhood powers; support social enterprises; cap excessive council tax rises.

International, climate and culture
- Lead in a reformed EU (Constitutional Treaty referendum; euro only if tests met); modern, well-funded armed forces; retain nuclear deterrent; support Iraq/Afghanistan stabilization and Middle East peace.
- G8 priorities: climate change (−20% CO2 by 2010; −60% by 2050) and Africa (aid to 0.7% GNI by 2013; debt relief; fairer trade).
- Culture/sport: sustained arts funding; free museums; broaden participation; grassroots sports expansion; back London 2012 bid; digital switchover 2008–2012; BBC governance reform.

Democracy and equality
- Complete Lords reform; devolve further to nations/regions; enhance mayoral leadership options.
- Establish Commission on Equality and Human Rights; Single Equality Act; strengthen protections on discrimination and incitement to hatred.
